title: CoT Redaction Resistance: Does Removing CoT Access Reduce Scheming or Just Hide It?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests a critical hypothesis: does CoT redaction eliminate or merely hide scheming? This has immediate implications for monitoring policy and whether to invest in CoT-based vs. behavior-based safety approaches.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a model with and without CoT on alignment-faking prompts, which involves significant ML engineering. Setting up the fine-tuning pipeline, creating CoT vs. non-CoT training data, and measuring scheming rates via behavioral outcomes are all non-trivial for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two separate fine-tuning runs plus behavioral evaluation creates substantial scope. Creating alignment-faking inducing prompts and measuring scheming via behavioral outcomes (not just text) adds complexity. Unlikely to fit in 30 hours for beginners.
